subject: math
title: Duration of Time: Converting Units, Elapsed Time, 24-Hour Time and Schedules
seo_title: Grade 5 Math: Elapsed Time Worksheets (Free, BC Curriculum, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on duration of time for the BC curriculum: convert seconds, minutes, hours, days and weeks, find elapsed time across noon and midnight, work out start and end times, use 24-hour time, and read BC Ferries and SkyTrain timetables. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count on in jumps: to the next o’clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left.
key_sub: 1 hour = 60 minutes, not 100, so do not subtract clock times like ordinary numbers. 1 day = 24 hours and 1 week = 7 days. At noon a.m. changes to p.m.; at midnight a new day starts.
body_html:
Units of time

Time does not count in tens and hundreds. Learn these facts:

UnitIs the same as
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes = 3600 seconds
1 day24 hours = 1440 minutes
1 week7 days = 168 hours
1 year12 months = 52 weeks and 1 day = 365 days (366 in a leap year)

To change a bigger unit into a smaller one, multiply: 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes. To change a smaller unit into a bigger one, take away groups: 210 minutes = 60 + 60 + 60 + 30 = 3 hours 30 minutes.

Example 1: conversion

How many hours are in 3 days?

1 day = 24 hours. 3 × 24 = 72.

Answer: 72 hours (not 36: a day is 24 hours, not 12)

Elapsed time: count on in jumps

Elapsed time is how much time passes from a start time to an end time. Draw an open time line. Jump to the next o’clock, then jump whole hours, then jump the minutes that are left. Add the jumps.

Example 2: across an hour

Swimming is from 4:50 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. How long is it?

4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes. 5:00 to 5:35 is 35 minutes. 10 + 35 = 45.

Answer: 45 minutes (not 85 minutes: 535 − 450 = 85 counts an hour as 100 minutes)

Finding the end time or the start time

To find an end time, add: first the hours, then the minutes. To find a start time, count back. At 12 noon, a.m. changes to p.m. At 12 midnight, p.m. changes to a.m. and a new day starts.

Example 3: end time

A movie starts at 6:50 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. When does it end?

Add 1 hour: 6:50 p.m. → 7:50 p.m. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 8:25 p.m.

Answer: 8:25 p.m.

Example 4: start time

A concert ends at 9:05 p.m. It lasted 1 hour 50 minutes. When did it start?

Count back 1 hour: 9:05 p.m. → 8:05 p.m. Then count back 50 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 45 minutes more is 7:15 p.m.

Answer: 7:15 p.m.

24-hour time

Ferry and SkyTrain timetables often use 24-hour time. The hours go from 00 to 23, so there is no a.m. or p.m. For p.m. times, add 12 to the hour: 4:35 p.m. = 16:35. Count on in jumps the same way. After 23:59 the clock goes back to 00:00.

Reading a timetable

Find the row for your trip, then read across. To find how long a trip takes, count on from the leaving time to the arriving time.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
08:47 to 09:04 worked out as 904 − 847 = 57 minutesAn hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on: 13 + 4 = 17 minutes
1 hour 15 minutes = 115 minutes1 hour = 60 minutes: 60 + 15 = 75 minutes
11:25 a.m. + 55 minutes = 12:20 a.m.After 12 noon the time is p.m.: 12:20 p.m.
9:45 + 30 minutes = 9:15 (forgot the new hour)45 + 30 = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes, so it is 10:15
16:35 read as 6:35 p.m.Take away 12: 16 − 12 = 4, so 4:35 p.m.
22:40 to 01:15 worked out as 22:40 − 01:15Count on past midnight: 20 minutes + 2 hours + 15 minutes
3 days = 36 hours1 day = 24 hours, not 12: 3 × 24 = 72 hours

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about time in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 5 math curriculum includes duration, using measurement of time. Students convert between units such as seconds, minutes, hours, days and weeks, and work out how long events last, including with 12-hour and 24-hour times and real schedules.

faq.q: What is the easiest way to work out elapsed time?
faq.a: Use an open time line and count on in jumps: to the next o’clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left. Adding the jumps is safer than subtracting the clock times.

faq.q: Why can’t you subtract times like ordinary numbers?
faq.a: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. So 09:04 − 08:47 is not 57 minutes; counting on gives 13 + 4 = 17 minutes.

faq.q: How do you find elapsed time across midnight?
faq.a: Count on to midnight first, then from midnight to the end time, and add the two parts. From 10:40 p.m. to 1:15 a.m. is 1 hour 20 minutes + 1 hour 15 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes.

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)

items.q: How many hours are in 1 day?
items.e: A day is 24 hours: 12 a.m. hours and 12 p.m. hours. 12 + 12 = 24. (Not 12: the hour hand goes around the clock twice in one day.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day, February 29, so it has 366. (52 is the number of weeks in a year. 360 uses 30 days in every month, but some months have 31.)

items.q: About how long does a BC Ferries trip from Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay take?
items.e: The ferry crosses the Strait of Georgia in a bit more than an hour and a half: about 1 hour 35 minutes. 1 minute 35 seconds is far too short, and days or weeks are far too long.

items.q: 4 hours = ? minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 minutes. (400 counts an hour as 100 minutes. 96 uses 24, but 24 is the hours in a day.)

items.q: 5 minutes = ? seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 5 × 60 = 300 seconds. (500 counts a minute as 100 seconds. 65 adds 60 + 5 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: 3 days = ? hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 3 × 24 = 72 hours. (36 uses 12 hours in a day. 180 uses 60.)

items.q: 6 weeks = ? days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 6 × 7 = 42 days. (30 counts only the 5 school days in each week. 13 adds 6 + 7.)

items.q: How many minutes are in three quarters of an hour?
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. (75 is three quarters of 100, but an hour is 60 minutes.)

items.q: 2 years = ? months
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. 2 × 12 = 24 months. (104 is the weeks in 2 years, and 730 is the days.)

items.q: 3 hours 25 minutes = ? minutes
items.e: 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes. 180 + 25 = 205 minutes. (325 counts an hour as 100 minutes. 145 counts only 2 hours.)

items.q: 210 minutes = ?
items.e: 60 + 60 + 60 = 180 minutes make 3 hours. 210 − 180 = 30 minutes left. So 210 minutes = 3 hours 30 minutes. (2 hours 10 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: 1 hour = ? seconds
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes and each minute = 60 seconds. 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds. (6000 uses 100 minutes in an hour. 120 adds 60 + 60.)

items.q: 400 seconds = ?
items.e: 6 × 60 = 360 seconds make 6 minutes. 400 − 360 = 40 seconds left. So 400 seconds = 6 minutes 40 seconds. (4 minutes counts a minute as 100 seconds.)

items.q: How many hours are in 1 week?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days and each day = 24 hours. 7 × 24 = 168 hours. (84 uses 12 hours in a day. 31 adds 7 + 24.)

items.q: Arjun’s family camps on Vancouver Island for 3 weeks 4 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. 21 + 4 = 25 days. (19 uses 5 days in a week. 34 uses 10 days in a week.)

items.q: Which is longer: 2 hours 10 minutes or 125 minutes?
items.e: 2 hours 10 minutes = 60 + 60 + 10 = 130 minutes. 130 is more than 125, so 2 hours 10 minutes is longer, by 5 minutes. (2 hours 10 minutes is not 210 minutes.)

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: 1 hour 45 minutes, 100 minutes, 1 hour 30 minutes.
items.e: Change everything to minutes. 1 hour 30 minutes = 90, 100 minutes = 100, 1 hour 45 minutes = 105. So the order is 1 hour 30 minutes, 100 minutes, 1 hour 45 minutes. (100 minutes is not 1 hour: it is 1 hour 40 minutes.)

items.q: 100 hours = ?
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. 4 × 24 = 96 hours make 4 days. 100 − 96 = 4 hours left. So 100 hours = 4 days 4 hours. (1 day thinks a day has 100 hours. 8 days 4 hours uses 12 hours in a day.)

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 day?
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours = 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes. Each minute is 60 seconds: 1440 × 60 = 86 400 seconds. (1440 is the minutes in a day, not the seconds. 144 000 uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

sets.title: Elapsed time within and across hours

items.q: Recess starts at 10:15 a.m. and ends at 10:32 a.m. How long is recess?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 32 − 15 = 17 minutes.

items.q: Library time is from 1:05 p.m. to 1:48 p.m. How long is library time?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour: 48 − 5 = 43 minutes.

items.q: Music class is from 9:35 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. How long is music class?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. is 20 minutes. 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Nadia’s swimming lesson is from 4:50 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 4:50 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 5:00 p.m. to 5:35 p.m. is 35 minutes. 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Salmon cooks on the barbecue from 5:38 p.m. to 6:21 p.m. How long does it cook?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:38 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 22 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 6:21 p.m. is 21 minutes. 22 minutes + 21 minutes = 43 minutes. (Not 83 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Lunch is from 11:48 a.m. to 12:25 p.m. How long is lunch?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 11:48 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 12 minutes; 12:00 noon to 12:25 p.m. is 25 minutes. 12 minutes + 25 minutes = 37 minutes. (Not 77 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The Terry Fox Run at school starts at 10:35 a.m. Olivia finishes at 11:22 a.m. How long does she take?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 10:35 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 25 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 11:22 a.m. is 22 minutes. 25 minutes + 22 minutes = 47 minutes. (Not 87 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Ji-woo hikes the Grouse Grind from 8:47 a.m. to 10:22 a.m. How long is the hike?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 8:47 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 13 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 1 hour; 10:00 a.m. to 10:22 a.m. is 22 minutes. 1 hour + 13 minutes + 22 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 1 hour 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Ava’s soccer practice is from 5:45 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 5:45 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 15 minutes; 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 7:00 p.m. to 7:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 10 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes. (Not 1 hour 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A movie starts at 6:55 p.m. and ends at 9:10 p.m. How long is the movie?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:55 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 5 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 9:00 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 5 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (Not 2 hours 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A lacrosse game is from 6:40 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. How long is the game?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 6:40 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 20 minutes; 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. is 1 hour; 8:00 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. is 55 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 55 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. (20 minutes + 55 minutes = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes.)

items.q: Hana’s snowboard lesson at Whistler is from 10:45 a.m. to 1:15 p.m. How long is the lesson?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 10:45 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 15 minutes; 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 2 hours; 1:00 p.m. to 1:15 p.m. is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 15 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. (Not 9 hours 30 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 10:45 − 1:15. Count on past 12 noon instead.)

items.q: A kayak tour on the Fraser River is from 9:50 a.m. to 12:35 p.m. How long is the tour?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 9:50 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 10 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 2 hours; 12:00 noon to 12:35 p.m. is 35 minutes. 2 hours + 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes. (Not 2 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A class field trip to Science World is from 9:20 a.m. to 2:05 p.m. How long is the trip?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 9:20 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 40 minutes; 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 4 hours; 2:00 p.m. to 2:05 p.m. is 5 minutes. 4 hours + 40 minutes + 5 minutes = 4 hours 45 minutes. (Not 7 hours 15 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 9:20 − 2:05. Count on past 12 noon instead.)

items.q: Jasleen’s family drives from Vancouver to Kelowna. They leave at 7:25 a.m. and arrive at 12:10 p.m. How long is the drive?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 7:25 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. is 35 minutes; 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 4 hours; 12:00 noon to 12:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 4 hours + 35 minutes + 10 minutes = 4 hours 45 minutes. (Not 4 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: The school day is from 8:40 a.m. to 2:58 p.m. How long is the school day?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 8:40 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 20 minutes; 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 5 hours; 2:00 p.m. to 2:58 p.m. is 58 minutes. 5 hours + 20 minutes + 58 minutes = 6 hours 18 minutes. (20 minutes + 58 minutes = 78 minutes = 1 hour 18 minutes.) (Not 5 hours 42 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 8:40 − 2:58. Count on past 12 noon instead.)

items.q: A charity skate-a-thon runs from 3:35 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. How long does it run?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 3:35 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 25 minutes; 4:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. is 5 hours; 9:00 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 5 hours + 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 5 hours 35 minutes. (Not 5 hours 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A hockey tournament runs from 7:40 a.m. to 3:25 p.m. How long does it run?
items.e: The time goes past 12 noon, from a.m. to p.m. Count on in jumps: 7:40 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. is 20 minutes; 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 7 hours; 3:00 p.m. to 3:25 p.m. is 25 minutes. 7 hours + 20 minutes + 25 minutes = 7 hours 45 minutes. (Not 4 hours 15 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 7:40 − 3:25. Count on past 12 noon instead.)

items.q: The power goes out at 11:40 p.m. It comes back on at 2:15 a.m. the next morning. How long is the power out?
items.e: The time goes past 12 midnight, from p.m. to a.m. Count on in jumps: 11:40 p.m. to 12:00 midnight is 20 minutes; 12:00 midnight to 2:00 a.m. is 2 hours; 2:00 a.m. to 2:15 a.m. is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes. (Not 9 hours 25 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 11:40 − 2:15. Count on past midnight instead.)

items.q: On a camping trip, Chloe falls asleep at 9:50 p.m. and wakes up at 6:35 a.m. the next morning. How long does she sleep?
items.e: The time goes past 12 midnight, from p.m. to a.m. Count on in jumps: 9:50 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. is 10 minutes; 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. is 8 hours; 6:00 a.m. to 6:35 a.m. is 35 minutes. 8 hours + 10 minutes + 35 minutes = 8 hours 45 minutes. (Not 3 hours 15 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 9:50 − 6:35. Count on past midnight instead.)

sets.title: Finding the start time or the end time

items.q: Recess starts at 10:20 a.m. It lasts 25 minutes. What time does recess end?
items.e: Add 25 minutes: 10:45 a.m.

items.q: The school bus leaves at 8:35 a.m. The ride takes 40 minutes. What time does it get to school?
items.e: Add 40 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 9:00 a.m., and 15 minutes more is 9:15 a.m.

items.q: Art class ends at 3:10 p.m. It lasted 35 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 3:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 2:35 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 3:10 p.m.)

items.q: Noah starts a science project at 1:45 p.m. and works for 50 minutes. What time does he stop?
items.e: Add 50 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 2:00 p.m., and 35 minutes more is 2:35 p.m.

items.q: School starts at 8:45 a.m. Ethan’s bus ride takes 50 minutes. What time must he get on the bus?
items.e: Count back 50 minutes: 45 minutes takes you to 8:00 a.m., and 5 minutes more is 7:55 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 8:45 a.m.)

items.q: Gym class starts at 11:25 a.m. It lasts 55 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 55 minutes: 35 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 20 minutes more is 12:20 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: Lunch is ready at 12:15 p.m. The soup cooked for 40 minutes. What time did it start cooking?
items.e: Count back 40 minutes: 15 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 25 minutes more is 11:35 a.m. Counting back past 12 noon changes p.m. to a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 12:15 p.m.)

items.q: A movie starts at 6:50 p.m. It lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 6:50 p.m. → 7:50 p.m. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 25 minutes more is 8:25 p.m.

items.q: Early hockey practice ends at 7:30 a.m. It lasted 1 hour 15 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 7:30 a.m. → 6:30 a.m. Then count back 15 minutes: 6:15 a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 7:30 a.m.)

items.q: It is 10:38 p.m. How long is it until 12:00 midnight?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 10:38 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. is 22 minutes; 11:00 p.m. to 12:00 midnight is 1 hour. 1 hour + 22 minutes = 1 hour 22 minutes. (Not 1 hour 62 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A field trip to Stanley Park starts at 9:40 a.m. It lasts 2 hours 45 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 9:40 a.m. → 11:40 a.m. Then add 45 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00 noon, and 25 minutes more is 12:25 p.m. The time goes past 12 noon, so it changes from a.m. to p.m.

items.q: A concert ends at 9:05 p.m. It lasted 1 hour 50 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 1 hour: 9:05 p.m. → 8:05 p.m. Then count back 50 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 8:00 p.m., and 45 minutes more is 7:15 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 9:05 p.m.)

items.q: Bread rises from 2:20 p.m. for 100 minutes. What time is it ready?
items.e: 100 minutes is not 1 hour: 100 = 60 + 40, so it is 1 hour 40 minutes. Add 1 hour: 2:20 p.m. → 3:20 p.m. Then add 40 minutes: 4:00 p.m. (3:20 p.m. counts 100 minutes as 1 hour.)

items.q: Kai’s family leaves for Whistler at 7:55 a.m. The trip takes 3 hours 25 minutes with stops. What time do they arrive?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 7:55 a.m. → 10:55 a.m. Then add 25 minutes: 5 minutes takes you to 11:00 a.m., and 20 minutes more is 11:20 a.m.

items.q: A whale-watching tour gets back to Victoria at 1:20 p.m. It lasted 2 hours 35 minutes. What time did it start?
items.e: Count back 2 hours: 1:20 p.m. → 11:20 a.m. Then count back 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 11:00 a.m., and 15 minutes more is 10:45 a.m. Counting back past 12 noon changes p.m. to a.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 1:20 p.m.)

items.q: A ringette tournament ends at 4:00 p.m. The last game lasted 135 minutes. What time did the last game start?
items.e: 135 minutes = 60 + 60 + 15 = 2 hours 15 minutes. Count back 2 hours: 4:00 p.m. → 2:00 p.m. Then count back 15 minutes: 1:45 p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 4:00 p.m.) (2:25 p.m. reads 135 minutes as 1 hour 35 minutes.)

items.q: The New Year’s Eve fireworks show in Vancouver starts at 11:35 p.m. Zara watches for 40 minutes. What time does she stop watching?
items.e: Add 40 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 12:00 midnight, and 15 minutes more is 12:15 a.m. The time goes past 12 midnight, so it changes from p.m. to a.m.

items.q: Harjot’s family starts driving to Prince George at 9:30 p.m. The drive takes 3 hours 50 minutes before they stop to rest. What time do they stop?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 9:30 p.m. → 12:30 a.m. Then add 50 minutes: 30 minutes takes you to 1:00 a.m., and 20 minutes more is 1:20 a.m. The time goes past 12 midnight, so it changes from p.m. to a.m.

items.q: A bus arrives in Vancouver at 6:10 a.m. after an overnight trip of 7 hours 25 minutes. What time did it leave?
items.e: Count back 7 hours: 6:10 a.m. → 11:10 p.m. Then count back 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 11:00 p.m., and 15 minutes more is 10:45 p.m. Counting back past 12 midnight changes a.m. to p.m. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 6:10 a.m.)

items.q: A salmon pie bakes for 1 hour 10 minutes and then cools for 25 minutes. Dinner is at 6:30 p.m. What is the latest time the pie can go in the oven?
items.e: Add the times first: 1 hour 10 minutes + 25 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. Count back from 6:30 p.m.: 1 hour → 5:30 p.m. 30 minutes → 5:00 p.m. 5 more minutes → 4:55 p.m. (5:20 p.m. forgets the cooling time. 8:05 p.m. adds instead of counting back.)

items.q: Write 16:35 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: Hours from 13 to 23 are p.m. times. Take away 12: 16 − 12 = 4. So 16:35 is 4:35 p.m. (Not 6:35 p.m.: do not just drop the 1. 16 − 12 = 4, not 6.)

items.q: Write 9:20 p.m. in 24-hour time.
items.e: p.m. times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 9 + 12 = 21. So 9:20 p.m. is 21:20. (09:20 is in the morning.)

items.q: Write 00:45 as a 12-hour time.
items.e: 00 is the hour just after midnight. In 12-hour time that hour is 12 a.m. So 00:45 is 12:45 a.m., 45 minutes after midnight. (12:45 p.m. is 45 minutes after noon.)

items.q: Write 12:10 p.m. in 24-hour time.
items.e: 12:10 p.m. is 10 minutes after noon. Noon is 12:00 in 24-hour time, so do not add 12. It is 12:10. (00:10 is 10 minutes after midnight.)

items.q: A ferry sails from 09:40 to 11:15. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 09:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes; 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour; 11:00 to 11:15 is 15 minutes. 1 hour + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 1 hour 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A soccer tournament runs from 13:25 to 16:10. How long does it run?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 13:25 to 14:00 is 35 minutes; 14:00 to 16:00 is 2 hours; 16:00 to 16:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 35 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 45 minutes. (Not 2 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Sofia’s family visits the Vancouver Aquarium from 14:50 to 18:05. How long is the visit?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 14:50 to 15:00 is 10 minutes; 15:00 to 18:00 is 3 hours; 18:00 to 18:05 is 5 minutes. 3 hours + 10 minutes + 5 minutes = 3 hours 15 minutes. (Not 3 hours 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A ferry leaves at 14:35. The trip takes 2 hours 50 minutes. What time does it arrive?
items.e: Add 2 hours: 14:35 → 16:35. Then add 50 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 17:00, and 25 minutes more is 17:25.

items.q: A ferry arrives at 13:10 after a trip of 2 hours 25 minutes. What time did it leave?
items.e: Count back 2 hours: 13:10 → 11:10. Then count back 25 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 11:00, and 15 minutes more is 10:45. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 13:10.)

items.q: A train leaves at 08:35 and arrives at 15:20. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:35 to 09:00 is 25 minutes; 09:00 to 15:00 is 6 hours; 15:00 to 15:20 is 20 minutes. 6 hours + 25 minutes + 20 minutes = 6 hours 45 minutes. (Not 6 hours 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A hockey game on TV is on from 17:48 to 20:30. How long is it on?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 17:48 to 18:00 is 12 minutes; 18:00 to 20:00 is 2 hours; 20:00 to 20:30 is 30 minutes. 2 hours + 12 minutes + 30 minutes = 2 hours 42 minutes. (Not 2 hours 82 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A concert starts at 19:40 and lasts 3 hours 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 3 hours: 19:40 → 22:40. Then add 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 23:00, and 15 minutes more is 23:15.

items.q: An electric bike charges from 18:40 to 21:05. How many minutes is that?
items.e: 18:40 to 19:00 is 20 minutes. 19:00 to 21:00 is 2 hours = 120 minutes. 21:00 to 21:05 is 5 minutes. 20 + 120 + 5 = 145 minutes. (265 subtracts the clock numbers: 2105 − 1840 = 265, as if an hour had 100 minutes.)

items.q: A SkyTrain trip starts at 11:50. Lucas rides and walks for 95 minutes in all. What time does he get there?
items.e: 95 minutes = 60 + 35 = 1 hour 35 minutes. Add 1 hour: 11:50 → 12:50. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes takes you to 13:00, and 25 minutes more is 13:25. (12:45 reads 95 minutes as 55 minutes.)

items.q: Which lasts longer: a game from 10:45 to 12:30, or a game from 15:50 to 17:30?
items.e: 10:45 to 12:30: 15 minutes + 1 hour + 30 minutes = 1 hour 45 minutes. 15:50 to 17:30: 10 minutes + 1 hour + 30 minutes = 1 hour 40 minutes. So 10:45 to 12:30 is longer, by 5 minutes. (“15:50 to 17:30, by 35 minutes” counts it as 2 hours 20 minutes: 17 − 15 = 2 and 50 − 30 = 20. But 17:30 is not 2 full hours after 15:50.)

items.q: Wei is at a ski camp on Grouse Mountain from 06:55 to 19:10. How long is that?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 06:55 to 07:00 is 5 minutes; 07:00 to 19:00 is 12 hours; 19:00 to 19:10 is 10 minutes. 12 hours + 5 minutes + 10 minutes = 12 hours 15 minutes. (Not 12 hours 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: A plane leaves Vancouver at 22:40 and lands at 01:15 the next morning (Vancouver time). How long is the flight?
items.e: The time goes past midnight (00:00). Count on in jumps: 22:40 to 23:00 is 20 minutes; 23:00 to 01:00 is 2 hours; 01:00 to 01:15 is 15 minutes. 2 hours + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes. (Not 21 hours 25 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 22:40 − 01:15. Count on past midnight (00:00) instead.)

items.q: A bus leaves Kamloops at 22:30. The trip takes 4 hours 15 minutes. What time does it arrive?
items.e: Add 4 hours: 22:30 → 02:30. Then add 15 minutes: 02:45. After 23:59 the clock starts again at 00:00, so there is no 26:45.

items.q: A night shift at the hospital is from 23:20 to 06:45 the next morning. How long is the shift?
items.e: The time goes past midnight (00:00). Count on in jumps: 23:20 to 00:00 is 40 minutes; 00:00 to 06:00 is 6 hours; 06:00 to 06:45 is 45 minutes. 6 hours + 40 minutes + 45 minutes = 7 hours 25 minutes. (40 minutes + 45 minutes = 85 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes.) (Not 16 hours 35 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 23:20 − 06:45. Count on past midnight (00:00) instead.)

items.q: Mateo’s bus arrives in Prince George at 07:20 after a trip of 9 hours 40 minutes. What time did it leave the evening before?
items.e: Count back 9 hours: 07:20 → 22:20. Then count back 40 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 22:00, and 20 minutes more is 21:40. (Count back to find a start time. Adding gives a time after 07:20.)

sets.title: Schedules and word problems: BC Ferries and SkyTrain

items.q: The ferry leaves Swartz Bay at 13:00. What time does it arrive in Tsawwassen?
items.e: Find 13:00 in the “Leaves Swartz Bay” column. Look across that row: it arrives at 14:35. (12:35 and 16:35 are on other rows.)

items.q: How long does the ferry take to go from Swartz Bay to Tsawwassen?
items.e: Take any row, such as 13:00 to 14:35. Count on in jumps: 13:00 to 14:00 is 1 hour; 14:00 to 14:35 is 35 minutes. 1 hour + 35 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes.

items.q: How long does the train take from Waterfront to Metrotown?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:47 to 09:00 is 13 minutes; 09:00 to 09:04 is 4 minutes. 13 minutes + 4 minutes = 17 minutes. (Not 57 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Leah arrives in Tsawwassen at 6:35 p.m. Which sailing did she take from Swartz Bay?
items.e: 6:35 p.m. in 24-hour time is 6 + 12 = 18, so 18:35. Find 18:35 in the “Arrives” column. That ferry leaves Swartz Bay at 17:00. (Not 15:00: that ferry arrives at 16:35, which is 4:35 p.m.)

items.q: How long is the whole ride, from Waterfront to King George?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:47 to 09:00 is 13 minutes; 09:00 to 09:26 is 26 minutes. 13 minutes + 26 minutes = 39 minutes. (Not 79 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Arjun’s family must be in Tsawwassen by 4:00 p.m. What is the latest ferry they can take from Swartz Bay?
items.e: 4:00 p.m. is 16:00. Look down the “Arrives” column for the last time before 16:00: 14:35. That ferry leaves at 13:00. (The 15:00 ferry arrives at 16:35, too late. 14:35 is an arrival time, not a sailing.)

items.q: Jasleen has hockey practice 3 times a week. Each practice is 1 hour 15 minutes. How much practice is that in one week?
items.e: 3 × 1 hour = 3 hours. 3 × 15 minutes = 45 minutes. Together: 3 hours 45 minutes. (3 hours 15 minutes forgets to multiply the minutes by 3.)

items.q: How long does the train take from Commercial–Broadway to New Westminster?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 08:56 to 09:00 is 4 minutes; 09:00 to 09:11 is 11 minutes. 4 minutes + 11 minutes = 15 minutes. (Not 55 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: Nadia gets to the Swartz Bay terminal at 10:05, just after the 09:00 ferry has left. How long must she wait for the next ferry?
items.e: Count on: 10:05 to 11:00 is 55 minutes. So it is 55 minutes. (Not 95 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the clock numbers.)

items.q: One summer, a ferry on the Inside Passage leaves Port Hardy at 07:30 and arrives in Prince Rupert at 23:30 the same day. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on in jumps: 07:30 to 08:00 is 30 minutes; 08:00 to 23:00 is 15 hours; 23:00 to 23:30 is 30 minutes. 15 hours + 30 minutes + 30 minutes = 16 hours. (30 minutes + 30 minutes = 60 minutes = 1 hour.) (Not 4 hours: 23:30 is 11:30 p.m., not 11:30 a.m.)

items.q: Ethan’s swim practice is 1 hour 25 minutes. Kai’s swim practice is 95 minutes. Whose practice is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 25 minutes = 60 + 25 = 85 minutes. 95 − 85 = 10. So Kai’s practice is longer, by 10 minutes. (Ethan’s by 30 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes: 125 − 95 = 30.)

items.q: Ava gets off at King George and walks 12 minutes to a swim meet that starts at 09:45. How many minutes early is she?
items.e: The train gets to King George at 09:26. 09:26 + 12 minutes = 09:38. 09:38 to 09:45 is 7 minutes. (19 minutes forgets the walk. 31 minutes adds the walk instead of taking it away.)

items.q: Olivia’s family takes the 15:00 ferry from Swartz Bay. When they get off in Tsawwassen, they drive 50 minutes home to Surrey. What time do they get home, in 12-hour time?
items.e: The 15:00 ferry arrives at 16:35. 16:35 + 50 minutes: 25 minutes takes you to 17:00, and 25 more is 17:25. 17 − 12 = 5, so it is 5:25 p.m. (Not 7:25 p.m.: 17:25 is 5:25 p.m., not 7:25 p.m. 4:25 p.m. forgets to carry the new hour.)

items.q: Chloe practises piano for 25 minutes every day for 2 weeks. How long is that in all?
items.e: 2 weeks = 14 days. 14 × 25 = 350 minutes. 5 × 60 = 300, and 350 − 300 = 50. So 350 minutes = 5 hours 50 minutes. (3 hours 50 minutes counts an hour as 100 minutes. 2 hours 55 minutes is only 1 week.)

items.q: Zara’s family drives overnight from Prince George to Vancouver. They leave at 9:25 p.m. and arrive at 5:40 a.m. How long is the drive?
items.e: The drive goes past 12 midnight. Count on in jumps: 9:25 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. is 35 minutes; 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. is 7 hours; 5:00 a.m. to 5:40 a.m. is 40 minutes. 7 hours + 35 minutes + 40 minutes = 8 hours 15 minutes. (35 minutes + 40 minutes = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes.) (Not 3 hours 45 minutes: that takes the smaller clock time from the bigger one, 9:25 − 5:40. Count on past midnight instead.)

items.q: Ji-woo’s family wants to be at Swartz Bay 45 minutes before the 11:00 ferry. The drive from Victoria takes 35 minutes. What is the latest time they can leave home?
items.e: They must be at the terminal by 11:00 − 45 minutes = 10:15. Count back the drive: 10:15 − 15 minutes = 10:00, and 20 more minutes back is 09:40. (10:15 forgets the drive. 10:25 forgets the 45 minutes at the terminal. 12:20 adds instead of counting back.)

items.q: Hana takes this train from Waterfront to Metrotown. She shops for 2 hours 30 minutes, then rides back to Waterfront. The ride back takes the same time. What time does she get back?
items.e: Hana arrives at Metrotown at 09:04. Add 2 hours 30 minutes: 11:34. The ride takes 17 minutes (08:47 to 09:04). 11:34 + 17 minutes = 11:51, because 34 + 17 = 51. (11:34 forgets the ride back. 11:17 starts the shopping at 08:47, before the train ride.)

items.q: At a soccer tournament, a team plays 3 games. Each game lasts 50 minutes, and there is a 15-minute break between games. The first game starts at 8:45 a.m. What time does the last game end?
items.e: Game 1: 8:45 to 9:35. Break: to 9:50. Game 2: to 10:40. Break: to 10:55. Game 3: to 11:45 a.m. There are only 2 breaks, because the breaks are between games. (11:15 a.m. forgets the breaks. 12:00 noon adds 3 breaks.)

items.q: School runs from 8:45 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., 5 days a week. How long is Liam at school in one week?
items.e: One day: 8:45 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 15 minutes, and 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 6 hours, so 6 hours 15 minutes. 5 days: 5 × 6 hours = 30 hours and 5 × 15 minutes = 75 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes. 30 hours + 1 hour 15 minutes = 31 hours 15 minutes. (6 hours 15 minutes is only one day. 30 hours 15 minutes forgets to multiply the minutes by 5.)

items.q: Noah’s family camps at a provincial park from Friday at 4:00 p.m. to Sunday at 11:00 a.m. How long is the camping trip?
items.e: Friday 4:00 p.m. to Saturday 4:00 p.m. is 1 day = 24 hours. Saturday 4:00 p.m. to Sunday 4:00 a.m. is 12 hours, and on to 11:00 a.m. is 7 more. 24 + 12 + 7 = 43 hours. (55 hours reads 4:00 p.m. as 4:00 a.m. 31 hours uses 12 hours in a day.)
